display_information.name: Quorly
display_information.long_description:
Quorly turns invoice approvals into a conversation — and makes sure a real human is behind every one.

*How it works*

• A contractor DMs Quorly an invoice PDF. Quorly reads it and pulls out the amount, invoice number, and description.
• It routes the invoice against your company's approval policy and pings only the people who actually have authority to approve it.
• Above a dollar threshold, the approver must pass a live World ID Selfie Check before their approval counts.
• Once the quorum is met, a Privy treasury wallet releases the payment onchain — under spend rules enforced inside a secure enclave.

*Ask it anything*

Mention @Quorly in a channel or just message it. It answers from your own invoices: what is waiting on you, where a payment got to, why you cannot approve something. It hands you a link straight into the approval, and it will tell you when it does not know rather than guess.

*Why the selfie check*

Today "approve" is a button click authenticated by a Slack session. A stolen laptop or a hijacked cookie can click it. Quorly makes the human in the loop provably live, at the moment money moves.

Each proof is bound to one invoice and one approver, expires in minutes, and can never be reused. No proof, a stale proof, or a reused proof means the approval simply doesn't record.

*Approvals scale with risk*

• Under $500 — one approval, no biometric check
• $500 to $5,000 — one approval with a live selfie check
• Above $5,000 — two approvers, each with a selfie check under three minutes old

Nobody can approve their own invoice, and every decision lands in an append-only audit trail: who approved, what proved it, and which transaction settled it.

*Commands*

• DM Quorly an invoice PDF to file it
• Mention @Quorly, or DM it, to ask about anything
• `/quorly pending` — open invoices
• `/quorly team` — the roster and who can approve
• `/quorly wallet` — your address and what it holds
• `/quorly treasury` — what the company can pay from
• `/quorly policy` — the tiers and what each one demands
• `/quorly whoami` — which seat you hold here

Face-verified invoice approvals and stablecoin payouts, in Slack.
